map_info.name: Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace
map_info.title: Carry the point through
map_info.description: Return to the held black point as a source of thrust. Aim the two spheres down or back and hold the triggers; release stops thrust while motion and gravity continue. The existing local-field crossing compares cube and visitor receiver contracts. In the final court the mortar, pad, moving platform, hinge, springs and loose cubes return as a space for combinations. The tutorial owns only the thrust-point-to-player connection. Wear the body visor to compare world velocity, thrust per unit mass and gravity. Turn your head without changing the world vector, then release the triggers: thrust stops before motion does. The visor reads this same connection; it adds no second movement model. The flying-mat circuit returns those same two trigger-thrust points at four raised gates. The mat is a visual carrier of the player movement model; release stops thrust while gravity remains. The mortar now has nine posts and its controls face the approach.

intro.text: Two routes over a pit. Aim the local field, test a cube, then enter. Inside, the field owns locomotion; the plank remains.
intro.speaker: Act V

truth_machine.text: The machine posts one vector into the field over the void. Down, and things fall; up-and-across, and they're carried over.
truth_machine.speaker: Vector machine

truth_void.text: Zero acceleration does not mean zero velocity. What motion did you bring into this place?
truth_void.speaker: The void

truth_complete.text: What carried you: the plank, your incoming motion, or the field? Where did ordinary walking take over again?
truth_complete.speaker: Reflection

documentation.layout: One primary encounter, spaced comparisons, a clear perimeter route. See the curation manifest for lesson roles.
